item.title: Escherichia coli hns and methylglyoxal link gut microbial metabolism to host neuronal gene regulation in Parkinson's disease
item.description: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuron loss in the substantia nigra (SN). Although the gut microbiota has been implicated in PD pathogenesis, how defined bacterial genes and their metabolites influence host neuronal gene regulation remains unclear. Here, we identify a gut microbial hns-methylglyoxal (MG) pathway linking Escherichia coli (E. coli) metabolism to host neuronal gene regulation. In the stool metagenomic cohort, hns, a...

item.title: Cytokine-induced killer cells combined with temozolomide suppress glioblastoma progression in an orthotopic model and demonstrate clinical feasibility in recurrent glioblastoma
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Glioblastoma (GBM) remains an aggressive primary brain tumor with limited therapeutic options after recurrence. Cytokine-induced killer (CIK) cells are ex vivo-expanded cytotoxic lymphocytes with T-cell and natural killer-like properties. We evaluated CIK-cell-based therapy using an orthotopic LN229-luciferase GBM model and a retrospective cohort of patients with recurrent GBM.

item.title: G3BP1 reduction during cellular senescence promotes SVIL expression and selected senescence-associated phenotypes
item.description: RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) can regulate gene expression through multiple post-transcriptional mechanisms, including the control of mRNA stability. In this study, we identified the Ras GTPase-activating protein-binding protein 1 (G3BP1) as a post-transcriptional regulator of supervillin (SVIL) expression. G3BP1 protein levels were consistently reduced across multiple senescence models, whereas SVIL mRNA and SVIL protein levels were increased. RIP analysis showed that SVIL mRNA was associated...

item.title: Spatial compartmentalization shapes distinct germinal center states during respiratory viral infection
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings support a model in which lymph node microanatomy imprints a distinct mGC state, diversifying humoral immune architecture during respiratory viral infection.

item.title: Association of Perioperative Hematocrit With Postoperative Neurological Complications in Adults Undergoing Revascularization Surgery for Moyamoya Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Higher preoperative and postoperative hematocrit levels were associated with postoperative neurological complications after multivariable adjustment; however, because the timing of the postoperative measurement relative to the onset of complications was uncertain, postoperative hematocrit should not be interpreted as a predictive variable. Perioperative change in hematocrit showed a more complex exploratory pattern after accounting for baseline hematocrit, but this finding requires...

item.title: Immune-Responsive Bioinks Enable Vision-Guided In situ Robotic Bioprinting to Accelerate Diabetic Wound Healing
item.description: Chronic diabetic wounds remain a major clinical challenge because persistent inflammation, hypoxia, and immune dysregulation prevent the transition of macrophages from pro-inflammatory M1 states to pro-regenerative M2 phenotypes. Here, we report an immunomodulatory colloidal bioink that integrates zein-based oxygen-generating microparticles and human mesenchymal stem cells within a porous, mechanically robust matrix for adaptive in situ bioprinting. Implemented with the autonomous, intelligent,...

item.title: Ultrasound-Guided Peristyloid Hydrodissection for Eagle Syndrome With 5% Dextrose: A Technical Note Integrating Computed Tomography-Defined Anatomy, Doppler Vascular Mapping, and Orthogonal Sonographic Guidance
item.description: Eagle syndrome is a symptomatic disorder associated with elongation or abnormal orientation of the styloid process and/or ossification of the stylohyoid complex. Clinical manifestations depend on the spatial relationship between the styloid complex and adjacent neural, muscular, fascial, and vascular structures. We describe an ultrasound-guided peristyloid hydrodissection technique using 5% dextrose in water (D5W) that integrates preprocedural computed tomography (CT), sequential landmark-based...

item.title: Persistent pneumothorax during pregnancy revealing histologically confirmed thoracic endometriosis
item.description: Thoracic endometriosis syndrome (TES) is the leading cause of catamenial pneumothorax but is rarely considered during pregnancy because ovulation and menstruation are physiologically suppressed. Consequently, persistent pneumothorax in pregnancy is commonly attributed to primary spontaneous pneumothorax, potentially delaying definitive diagnosis and treatment. We report a 31-year-old primigravida at 27 weeks' gestation who presented with persistent right-sided pneumothorax despite tube...

item.title: A New Genus of Myriangiales Order Isolated from a Toenail
item.description: Clarifying the phylogenetic positions of microorganisms is a primary area of expertise of microbial culture collection centers. In the present study, we aimed to elucidate the phylogenetic position of a fungal strain, previously reported from a human toenail. The earlier report was able to resolve its phylogeny only until genus level (Elsinoë). After being deposited in KACC as strain KACC 410304, a comprehensive examination was conducted which included studying its morphological features as well...

item.title: Normative data of the coding test in Korean middle-aged and elderly population
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The normative data presented in this study provide a valuable reference for clinicians and researchers to more accurately evaluate processing speed abilities in middle-aged and older Korean adults.

item.title: Determinants of Thoracic Reciprocal Change and Its Relationship to Proximal Junctional Kyphosis Following Lower Thoracic Fusion for Lumbar Flatback Deformity
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Thoracic RC after lower thoracic fusion is primarily determined by preoperative thoracic characteristics and the magnitude of lordosis correction. Although associated with an early increase in the postoperative junctional angle, thoracic RC itself does not independently predict the development of PJK. These findings suggest that thoracic RC appears to behave as a compensatory adaptation to sagittal realignment rather than an independent driver of PJK.

item.title: Posterior Osteophyte Resection from the Medial Femoral Condyle Increases Medial Gap of Extension and Mid-Flexion in Total Knee Arthroplasty
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Resection of large posterior osteophytes > 5 mm from the medial femoral condyle can be expected to result in a larger increase in the medial gap than resection of osteophytes ≤ 5 mm. Surgeons need to pay close attention to these intraoperative changes in the medial gap after posterior osteophyte resection to achieve appropriate mediolateral balance during TKA.

item.title: Effect of Hand Grip Exercise on Rotator Cuff Strength and Shoulder Function Recovery after Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Hand grip exercise affected the rotator cuff and periscapular muscle strengths at 6 months after rotator cuff repair. The grip exercises can effectively and safely promote a faster recovery of shoulder muscle strength and function, without compromising rotator cuff healing.

item.title: Second Ray Pathologies Associated with Hallux Valgus: A Radiographic Comparative Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: HV without radiographic features of midfoot instability tended to be associated with lesser MTP joint lesions, whereas HV with radiographic features of midfoot instability was more commonly associated with lesser TMT joint osteoarthritis. Further prospective longitudinal studies are required to clarify causal relationships among these associations.

item.title: Comparative Effects of Acellular Dermal Matrix and Atelocollagen Injections in Intratendinous Partial-Thickness Rotator Cuff Tears: A Retrospective Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Both ADM and atelocollagen injections were associated with clinically meaningful improvement in patients with intratendinous partial-thickness rotator cuff tears, with generally maintained MRI-based structural outcomes at follow-up.

item.title: Comparison of Mortality and Revision Rates between Cemented and Cementless Fixation in Bipolar Hemiarthroplasty: A Nationwide Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Cemented fixation had a higher risk of short-term mortality and adverse cardiac events after HA, while it had a lower risk of femoral stem revision and PPFs.

item.title: Timing of reduction glossoplasty and clinical outcomes in children with Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Reduction glossoplasty is a feasible treatment for children with BWS-associated macroglossia. Younger age at surgery was associated with a lower prevalence of malocclusion, whereas age at surgery was not significantly associated with postoperative complications. These findings support individualized surgical decision-making that balances potential dentofacial benefits against perioperative risks.

item.title: Radiologic Progression of Early-Stage Ankle Osteoarthritis: A Mean 12-Year Follow-up Observational Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this 12.1-year follow-up observational study of early-stage ankle OA, no radiographic progression was observed in 56.2% of ankles, 1-stage progression in 39.3%, and 2-stage progression in 4.5%. Progression from stage IIIA to stage IIIB occurred more frequently in ankles with hindfoot varus. Lower limb alignment and clinical factors (sex, age, and BMI) were not significantly associated with OA progression.

item.title: Decoding user satisfaction during reading of pre-defined question-answer pairs: BCI approach using delta and gamma EEG
item.description: INTRODUCTION: The rapid proliferation of large language models (LLMs) has intensified the need for robust evaluation frameworks to align artificial intelligence (AI) behavior with human expectations. While current reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) strategies heavily rely on explicit, post-hoc self-reports, these metrics are fundamentally limited by subjective biases and user non-compliance.

item.title: Valuing an urban marathon as a public sport service: evidence from the Seoul international marathon
item.description: This study examined the nonmarket value of the Seoul International Marathon (SIM) as part of the city's sport infrastructure and public sport service provision, using the Contingent Valuation Method (CVM) to estimate Seoul residents' willingness to pay for the event. An online survey of 1,250 adult residents employed a double-bounded dichotomous-choice format in a hypothetical tax-based donation scenario. A logit model was used to explore which factors shape willingness to pay, and bid level,...

item.title: Spatial robustness of P100 latency compared with amplitude: a data-driven rationale for visual pathway monitoring during neuroendovascular procedures
item.description: Intraoperative visual evoked potential (VEP) monitoring has a reputation for being unreliable, and much of that belongs to P100 amplitude. Amplitude shifts with electrode position, anesthetic depth, and dipole geometry. Practice has nonetheless tended to lean on amplitude, and to treat latency as the weaker of the two. Neuroendovascular procedures give reason to shift that emphasis. During open surgery there can be a mixture of direct and ischemic neural injury, whereas in an endovascular...

item.title: Which Injection Is More Effective for Partial-Thickness Rotator Cuff Tear? Atelocollagen Versus Acellular Dermal Matrix
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Compared with atelocollagen injection, ADM injection resulted in a superior improvement in rotator cuff tendon integrity. However, clinical outcomes were comparable between the groups.

item.title: Kinematic Alignment in Total Knee Arthroplasty: Unresolved Challenges and Barriers to Overcome for Universal Application
item.description: Restoring patient-specific alignment in total knee arthroplasty has emerged as a promising approach to improve joint kinematics and reduce the need for soft-tissue release. Kinematic alignment (KA) and its variants-including restricted, inverse, and functional alignment-seek to replicate the patient's native joint line obliquity (JLO) and pre-arthritic alignment, often guided by classification systems such as the Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee (CPAK). However, despite the theoretical...

item.title: Learning Curve for Biportal Endoscopic Transforaminal Lumbar Interbody Fusion in a Junior Endoscopic Spine Surgeon: A Phase-Specific Retrospective Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: BE-TLIF demonstrates a phase-specific learning curve, with proficiency achieved after sufficient case volume. Structured training focusing on decompression and cage insertion may accelerate skill acquisition. Comprehensive inclusion of multi-level cases and phase-specific time analysis provide a robust framework for evaluating technical proficiency in endoscopic spine surgery training.

item.title: Global evolutionary dynamics of peste des petits ruminants virus reveals geographic lineage structuring and clade-defining mutational signatures
item.description: Peste des petits ruminants virus (PPRV) is recognized as one of the most economically significant transboundary pathogens affecting small ruminants. However, despite the increasing availability of whole-genome sequences, comprehensive global analyses integrating evolutionary history, phylogeography, and genome-wide lineage-defining molecular markers remain limited. This study investigated the global genomic diversity, evolutionary history, and molecular characteristics of PPRV using whole-genome...

item.title: Transoral thyroidectomy in a consecutive cancer-enriched cohort of 1-000 patients: a single-surgeon experience with endoscopic and robotic platforms
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this large cancer-enriched single-surgeon cohort, transoral thyroidectomy was associated with acceptable perioperative outcomes in carefully selected patients. Although TOETVA and TORT showed differences in the overall cohort, adjusted differences were modest and did not establish superiority of either platform. Both approaches may retain practical value within an evolving transoral thyroidectomy practice.

item.title: Case Report: Epitheliotropic cutaneous presentation of multicentric diffuse large B-cell lymphoma in a dog
item.description: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most common histological subtype of canine multicentric lymphoma, whereas epitheliotropism is classically associated with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. A 9-year-old neutered male Chihuahua was diagnosed with stage IVb multicentric lymphoma and achieved complete remission with a UW-25 L-CHOP protocol. However, an upper lip mass, cytologically consistent with lymphoma, developed during remission. Electrochemotherapy was performed for local control and...

item.title: Three Decades of Socioeconomic Inequality in India's Breastfeeding Indicators, 1993-2021
item.description: Although existing literature heavily focuses on the health outcomes of exclusive breastfeeding (EBF) in India, studies addressing socioeconomic inequalities across a broad spectrum of breastfeeding indicators remain scarce. We utilized five waves of National Family Health Survey data (1993-2021) to analyze temporal trends and socioeconomic inequalities, proxied by maternal education (no formal schooling, 1st-5th grade, 6th-8th grade, 9th-12th grade, and above 12th grade) and household wealth...

item.title: Functionally declining microbiota in chronic disease: beyond taxonomic loss
item.description: Microbiota deterioration in modern human populations has been linked to chronic disease, and taxonomic profiling is increasingly used to understand, diagnose, and guide treatment. Yet such profiles do not fully capture disease-relevant microbiota states. I propose functional decline within retained taxa as a distinct axis of microbiota deterioration, complementary to taxonomic loss. Modern environmental pressures can drive not only taxonomic loss but also directional selection toward variants or...

item.title: CO<sub>2</sub> Capture in MOFs: Connecting Experiments, Multiscale Simulations, and Data-Driven Approaches
item.description: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising porous materials for CO(2) capture due to their tunable pore structures and chemically versatile adsorption sites. However, achieving efficient capture at low CO(2) concentrations while balancing adsorption strength, regeneration, and structural stability remains challenging. Existing reviews often treat experimental and computational investigations separately, limiting the development of unified design principles. This review integrates...

item.title: Transitional Nursing Care for Oesophageal Cancer Patients: A Scoping Review
item.description: CONCLUSION: Patients with oesophageal cancer require multifaceted, continuous transitional nursing care across the care continuum, yet current interventions inadequately address relational, social, and system-level needs. Evidence gaps exist between patients' experienced needs and available interventions, particularly in hospital-to-community care coordination and nonsurgical treatment pathways.

item.title: Modeling Logical Interdependencies: Quantifying Systemic Risk From Rule-Governed Actions
item.description: Systemic risk in critical infrastructure is often analyzed through physical, geographic, and cyber interdependencies. Yet infrastructures are also interdependent through the governing rules that organize human action. These rule-mediated connections are a form of logical interdependency, and breakdowns in rule-governed action can create pathways through which disruption spreads. This paper develops a framework for diagnosing and quantifying this underrecognized source of systemic risk. It does...

item.title: Pepper RING-type E3 ligase, CaANKR1, negatively regulates drought tolerance by modulating CaMAPK1 stability
item.description: Drought stress severely restricts plant growth and productivity, and abscisic acid (ABA)-mediated signaling plays a central role in coordinating adaptive responses to water deficit. Mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) cascades are widely involved in plant stress signaling; however, the ubiquitin-mediated regulation of MAPK stability during drought responses remains poorly understood. In this study, we conducted a yeast two-hybrid screening and identified CaMAPK1, a pepper (Capsicum annuum)...

item.title: The effects of intravenous glutamine supplementation in critically ill patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: IV glutamine supplementation was not associated with improved survival or overall infection rates in critically ill adults. Current evidence does not support routine IV glutamine supplementation in unselected critically ill patients.

item.title: Hydraulic Calcium Silicate Cement-Root Dentine Interfacial Layer
item.description: Understanding the interfacial layer (IFL) between hydraulic calcium silicate cements (CSCs) and root dentine is essential for optimising CSC performance and developing next-generation biomaterials. This scholarly review summarises current evidence on IFL composition, formation, structure, and clinical significance. item.title: Regional disparities in emergency retinal surgery: interregional transfer and visual disability in a nationwide population-based study in Korea
item.description: CONCLUSION: Despite universal health insurance, regional disparities in access to retinal surgery persist in Korea, with services concentrated in the Seoul metropolitan area. Transfer was independently associated with visual disability but not reoperation. The underlying mechanism likely involves referral of complex cases, patient preference, and transfer-related delay, although claims data cannot distinguish their relative contributions. item.title: Epigenetic-Targeting Regimens vs. Conventional Chemotherapy in Relapsed/Refractory PTCL: A Meta-Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Compared with CC, Epi-Rx may be associated with improved survival outcomes in R/R PTCL. Prospective comparative studies are warranted to confirm this finding.

item.title: Atropine-Associated Central Anticholinergic Syndrome during Carotid Artery Stenting: A Case Report
item.description: Acute neurobehavioral deterioration during carotid artery stenting (CAS) requires prompt evaluation for serious neurological complications. We report a patient in their 70s who developed profound hyperactive delirium approximately 15 minutes after receiving prophylactic intravenous atropine (0.25 mg) during CAS. The episode was characterized by severe agitation, bilateral mydriasis, and facial flushing without focal neurological deficits. Repeated angiography and subsequent neuroimaging showed...

item.description: CONCLUSION: These divergent findings raise the possibility that elevated circulating CCL2 levels in sarcopenia reflect a compensatory response to muscle deterioration rather than a direct pathogenic driver, highlighting the need for further mechanistic validation.

item.title: Targeting Cannabinoid 1 Receptor in Macrophages Alleviates Psoriatic Skin Inflammation Through the AUF1-NLRP3 Axis
item.description: Psoriasis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease associated with systemic metabolic dysregulation; however, the molecular pathways linking metabolic signaling to skin inflammation remain poorly understood. Here, we identify cannabinoid 1 receptor (CB1R) in macrophages as a key immunometabolic regulator of psoriatic inflammation and a potential therapeutic target. item.description: Catalytic oxidative cancer therapy exploits elevated hydrogen peroxide levels within tumor microenvironments to induce selective oxidative damage in malignant cells. However, many ROS-generating therapeutic systems rely on heavy metals or structurally complex inorganic architectures, limiting their biological compatibility and catalytic selectivity. item.title: Microbubble Timing and Vascular Geometry Are Associated With Vessel-Level Blood-Brain Barrier Opening During Focused Ultrasound
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Microbubble handling and injection-to-sonication timing are potential protocol variables in FUS-BBBO studies. Control-normalized extravascular metrics provide a reproducible framework for vessel-level longitudinal 2-photon quantification.

item.title: Preoperative transthoracic echocardiogram and delay to geriatric hip fracture surgery
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The available evidence did not demonstrate a statistically significant association between time to surgery and preoperative TTE. However, the data available are limited by heterogeneity, confounding and insufficient statistical power. In general, improving access to, and efficiency in TTE could help minimise delays to surgery, particularly in centres with limited resources. Strict adherence to American College of Cardiology guidelines for preoperative TTE indications is recommended.

item.title: Programmed photocontrol of polymer materials with multiple stimuli for fabrication and degradation
item.description: Light-induced synthesis, degradation, and processing of polymer materials are powerful technologies in materials science that exploit the exceptional spatiotemporal resolution of light to achieve precise material control. item.description: Over the past decade, biologic therapies targeting key inflammatory pathways have fundamentally transformed the treatment landscape for patients with chronic inflammatory airway diseases. item.description: We conducted a pharmacokinetic study to compare two fixed-dose combinations of ibuprofen/acetaminophen (IP-TA and IP-TB) with different formulation designs and excipient compositions, and explored how formulation differences influence ibuprofen pharmacokinetics by comparing in vitro dissolution and in vivo absorption profiles. item.description: Rectus sheath hematoma (RSH) is an uncommon cause of acute abdominal pain that predominantly affects older, anticoagulated adults and usually presents with a palpable abdominal-wall mass. We report a 17-year-old previously healthy male who developed midline lower abdominal pain after 6 days of severe coughing, without anticoagulation, trauma, or bleeding disorder, and with no visible swelling, ecchymosis, or palpable mass; Carnett's sign was positive. item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that verofilcon A may be associated with more favorable clinical signs of allergic conjunctivitis than narafilcon A in CL wearers with CL discomfort.

item.description: Objective: Managing heart failure requires simultaneous regulation of mean arterial pressure, cardiac output, and left atrial pressure, which is challenging due to complex cardiovascular interactions and limited monitoring. This study presents a proof-of-concept in-vivo evaluation of a discrete two-degree-of-freedom hemodynamic control system designed to regulate these three hemodynamic variables through titration of cardiovascular interventions under pulmonary artery catheter monitoring....

item.title: Risk stratification of Stage B heart failure with BNP levels of 35-100 pg/mL: development of the PHASE Index from the CHART-2 Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Patients with preclinical HF and BNP levels of 35-100 pg/mL exhibit substantial risk heterogeneity. The PHASE Index improves identification of high-risk individuals and provides a pragmatic tool for risk stratification beyond the conventional BNP threshold.

item.description: Contrast agents capable of being injected and cured in situ within the vasculature are required for angiography based on X-ray microcomputed tomography (µ-CT) for pathophysiology of biopsies or postmortem. item.description: Developing strategies for photocatalytic reduction of low-concentration CO(2) under ambient conditions is essential for mitigating global warming and addressing energy and carbon resource shortages. item.title: A new species of Zhangixalus (Anura, Rhacophoridae) from Lao Cai Province, Vietnam
item.description: A new treefrog species, Zhangixalus matsuii sp. nov., is described from Y Ty Commune, Lao Cai Province, northwestern Vietnam. The new species is diagnosed by the following characteristics: size medium (SVL 35.5-37.6 mm in males); dorsum olive green with many brown spots; axilla and groin grey with cream spots along flank; throat cream with grey spots; belly and ventral surface of hind limbs red-orange. The genetic distance between the new species and other species of Zhangixalus ranges from 2.5%...

item.title: Selective impairment in musical chord Reading in posterior cortical atrophy: A case study of integrative visual agnosia
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the diagnostic challenges clinicians face in recognizing visuoperceptual deficits in PCA. The individual's integrative visual agnosia, exemplified by her difficulty interpreting musical chords, offers valuable insight into how such deficits manifest in daily activities.

item.title: Geometric Tear Configuration Influences Intraoperative Reparability after Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: RC tear pattern was associated with intraoperative reparability after arthroscopic repair but did not independently predict postoperative structural healing. Anterior L-shaped tears demonstrated higher reparability than crescent-shaped tears, whereas retear rates were comparable. Tear pattern recognition may assist surgical planning rather than serve as a standalone prognostic factor for tendon healing.

item.title: Programmable Spatiotemporal Magnetic Fields for Selective Multimodal Actuation and Deterministic Decoupling of Heterogeneous Magnetic Robots
item.description: Magnetic milli/microrobots hold strong potential for biomedical applications, but their deployment as multi-robot systems is limited by short-range magnetic coupling, which prevents independent control in confined environments. item.title: Structural defects in male meiotic cell division lead to reproductive genome instability and disturbed microsporogenesis in banana (Musa spp.)
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study contributes to our understanding of how genomic determinants affect meiotic stability and male fertility in banana and can aid in high-throughput assessment of meiotic stability in banana on the mature pollen level.

item.title: Identifying facility-level and infrastructure-level bottlenecks in Japan's lecanemab rollout through an online survey of dementia specialists
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Japan's rollout may be constrained by some bottlenecks in diagnostics, infusion infrastructure, and uncompensated tasks. Appropriate policy interventions might help secure equitable access to the treatment.

item.title: Smaller pineal volume in Alzheimer's disease than in dementia with Lewy bodies
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Pineal volume was smaller in AD than in DLB; this difference may reflect the neuropathological characteristics specific to AD.

item.title: Language-supervised electrocardiogram interpretation with vision transformer
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate the feasibility of vision-language supervision from paired ECG recordings and summary reports for learning transferable ECG representations without task-specific supervised training. This framework provides a basis for future extension of vision-language learning to ECG images encountered in routine clinical practice.

item.description: Cobalt (Co) complexes of porphyrin derivatives possess distinctive redox properties, and hence, their development has attracted significant interest across a wide range of fields. item.description: Brain metastases are the most common intracranial tumor in adults, and most arise from lung, breast, or melanoma. We propose a conceptual framework organized around three requirements for colonization, each unevenly distributed across the brain: vascular access, metabolic substrate, and escape from immune surveillance. We organize the literature around this three-axis framework and argue that metabolism, though the least exploited clinically, is where personalization may deliver the largest...

item.title: Association between different types of tea consumption frequency and sleep quality with cognitive function among older adults in Qingdao rural area
item.description: CONCLUSION: Increased consumption frequency of green tea, alongside maintaining good sleep quality, is associated with enhanced cognitive function. These findings highlight the value of modifiable lifestyle factors in promoting cognitive health.

item.title: Association between transthyretin levels and Alzheimer's disease: A meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Lower TTR levels are significantly associated with AD. This finding suggests that TTR warrants further investigation as a candidate biomarker for AD, although prospective studies are needed to validate its clinical utility.

item.title: Comparison of Clinical, Hemodynamic and Imaging Profiles Between Isolated Pulmonary Vasculitis and Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension
item.description: Isolated pulmonary vasculitis (IPV) and chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) are important causes of pulmonary artery stenosis-related pulmonary hypertension. Differentiating between them remains challenging. item.title: Natural History of Rare Tumor Risk Syndromes: A Scoping Review to Inform Cost-Effectiveness Models
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The evidence base for RTRS is heterogeneous, particularly regarding longitudinal outcomes and comparative surveillance strategies. These limitations restrict the parameterization of disease progression models and the evaluation of the cost-effectiveness of surveillance strategies, leaving substantial uncertainty about optimal management strategies. item.title: Biodegradable ROS-Responsive TPCD Nanoparticles Mitigate Cisplatin-Induced Acute Kidney Injury via Synergistic Antioxidant and Immunomodulatory Actions
item.description: CONCLUSION: TPCD NPs demonstrate renoprotective effects in cisplatin-induced AKI, likely via combined antioxidant, anti-apoptotic, and immunomodulatory actions. However, the observed renal accumulation requires further quantitative pharmacokinetic validation, and long-term safety and efficacy in other AKI models remain to be established. This study suggests that TPCD NPs are a promising preclinical candidate for AKI, but clinical translation claims should be made with caution.
